rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s literal oil-related sense of d-h-n appears in the examples from al-Muʾminūn and al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: وفي القرآن من هذا المعنى الأول، آيتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhān derives from oil and figuratively means softening or lenience, as softening speech resembles softening oil.
rows.anchor: وبملحظ من التطرية والتلين جاءت الدلالة للإدهان، في اللين والتساهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mudāhana commonly describes ingratiation or cajoling involving deceit, or laxity and dereliction.
rows.anchor: وشاع استعمال المداهنة في المداجاة والملاطفة عن غش وخداع، أو عن تساهل وتفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphorical sense of idhān also occurs in al-Wāqiʿa 56:81, alongside this verse.
rows.anchor: وفي القرآن من هذه الدلالة امجازية، آيتان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported gloss is that the opponents wanted Muhammad to make concessions so they would reciprocate with concessions.
rows.anchor: قيل في تفسيرها: ودوا لو ترخص لهم فيرخصون لك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss is that they wished him to soften his religion so they would soften theirs.
rows.anchor: أو: ودوا لو تلين في دينك فيلينون في دينهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further gloss is that they wanted him to lean toward their gods and abandon the truth, so they could accommodate him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ودوا لو تركن إلى آلهتهم وتترك ما أنت عليه من الحق فيمالئونك

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the reading that they wished Muhammad to compromise in religion by leaning toward their gods, after which they would accommodate his worship of God.
rows.anchor: وقد نقلها الطبري ثم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī adduces 17:74, where Muhammad nearly leaned slightly toward the opponents, as support for his interpretation.
rows.anchor: واستأنس له بآية الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes idhān, the metaphor of softening speech, from mudāhana, which can mean accommodation and ingratiation.
rows.anchor: فالإدهان مأخوذ من الدهن، شبه التليين في القول بتليين الدهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle law conveys the opponents’ remote, frustrated wish; exegetes and grammarians instead fixated on the retained nūn in fayudhinūna and its inflectional rule.
rows.anchor: وشغل نحاة ومفسرون بعقد الصنعة الإعرابية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents are deluded if they think their wealth, status, and children mean they deserve honor or that God must preserve their blessings despite their disbelief; provision is a test.
rows.anchor: أي غرور غرهم بالخالق، أن يبقى عليهم ما آتاهم من نعمة يبتليهم بها فكفروا وجحدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is challenged to ask which of them guarantees that their claimed entitlement will remain theirs through the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ثم يتجه الخطاب إلى المصطفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions await no answer; their force is to humble the opponents, shatter their arrogance, confound them, and instruct anyone who can hear and see.
rows.anchor: وتمضي كل هذه الأسئلة لا تنتظر جواباً، وإنما حسب القرآن الكريم أن يواجههم بها على هذا الأسلوب البياني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author attaches the temporal phrase “the day” to the preceding command: let them bring their partners, if truthful, on the day the shin is uncovered.
rows.anchor: أي: فليأتوا بشركائهم، إن كانوا صادقين، يوم يكشف عن ساق

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report transmitted by al-Ṭabarī from Ibn Masʿūd through Abū al-Zaʿrāʾ says God appears and asks whom people worship; believers recognize and prostrate, while hypocrites’ backs become rigid and joined.
rows.anchor: فيقول: هل تعرفون ربكم؟ فيقولون: سبحانه إذا اعترف إلينا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also cites an Ibn Masʿūd report saying the Merciful uncovers His shin; believers prostrate and hypocrites’ backs become one rigid surface.
rows.anchor: ونقل "الزمخشري" من حديث ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls the interpretation as God’s literal leg one of the strangest reports and challenges the anthropomorphists who rely on it.
rows.anchor: وقد تعلقت المشبهة بهذا التأويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic usage, uncovering or tucking up the shin is a figurative expression for readiness, alarm, and the onset of severe hardship, especially war.
rows.anchor: فهل أعوزهم من بيان العربية أنها ألفت مثل هذا الاستعمال المجازي: الكشف عن الساق، أو التشمير عنها

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses uncovering the shin as an image of an approaching, destructive crisis.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: كشفت لهم عن ساقها وبدا من الشر البوارح

rows.speaker: حاتم الطائي
rows.claim: Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī’s line depicts war as biting back when it is pressed and as baring its shin when it intensifies.
rows.anchor: وقال حاتم الطائي: أخو الحرب إن غضت به الحرب عضها وإن شمرت عن ساقها الحرب شمرا

rows.speaker: ابن قيس الرقيات
rows.claim: Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt’s line has a woman’s attendants exposed when the crisis distracts the old man from his sons.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قيس الرقيات: تذهل الشيخ عن بنيه وتبدى عن خدام العقيلة العذراء

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: A rajaz poet’s line says war has bared its shin and urges people to gird themselves and exert effort.
rows.anchor: وقال الراجز: قد شمرت عن ساقها فشدوا وجدت الحرب بكم فجدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Judgment is an appalling hardship for disbelievers: they are called to prostrate as a belated rebuke after wasting their worldly chance, when they were safe and able.
rows.anchor: وأي شدة أفظع هولاً على الكافرين من يوم الحساب، حين يدعون إلى السجود تعجيزاً وتحسيراً وتقريعاً قد فاتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Physical explanations say the backbones lose their joints, the vertebrae fuse into one, or the body becomes rigid after a forty-year wait and a divine manifestation; the author rejects such elaborations as incompatible with the text and context.
rows.anchor: فذلك، ومثله كثير، مما لا يحتمله منهجنا في الأخذ بنص الآيات البينات، لفظاً وسياقاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inability to prostrate means the time for worship and the period of religious obligation have passed, rather than a bodily disability.
rows.anchor: والأولى أن يحمل العجز عن السجود على فوات أوان التعبد ومهلة التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The missed opportunity parallels al-Fajr’s scene of Hell brought forth and the sinner’s belated wish that he had prepared for his true life, after rejecting responsibility and loving wealth.
rows.anchor: ونظيره ما في آيات الفجر، في سياق الحديث عن مصير الطغاة والمفسدين في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This discourse” first refers to the words of God recited by the Prophet.
rows.anchor: الحديث المشار إليه في الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also allows that “this discourse” may mean the account of the afterlife in Sūrat al-Qalam.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ما جاء في سورة القلم من حديث الآخرة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān takes “this discourse” to refer to Sūrat al-Qalam’s account of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وهو ما ذهب إليه "أبو حيان"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istidrāj is taking someone gradually, step by step, while granting them respite.
rows.anchor: والاستدراج: الأخذ على إمهال درجة درجة

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains that God lets them enjoy worldly goods until they mistake this for divine favor and persist in tyranny, then seizes them suddenly.
rows.anchor: وقد فسره الإمام الطبري: وذلك بأن يمتعهم بمتاع الدنيا حتى يظنوا أنهم متعوا به بخير لهم عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra’s closing words support the Prophet and link back to its opening, which likewise affirms his freedom from madness and his great character.
rows.anchor: تأييداً للمصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام، يرتبط بما بدأت به السورة من مثل هذا التأييد الإلهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic literary study has long selected poetry and prose as models while neglecting the Qur’an, the greatest Arabic book and its enduring rhetorical miracle and model of expression.
rows.anchor: شغلنا بهذا ومثله عن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: University Arabic departments leave the Qur’an to tafsīr courses, with few attempts to bring it into rhetorical study alongside Arabic literary heritage.
rows.anchor: ونحن في الجامعة، نترك هذا الكنز الغالي لدرس التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Until roughly a quarter-century before writing, tafsīr teaching generally followed a traditional transmitted approach focused on understanding the text as earlier exegetes did.
rows.anchor: وكان المنهج المتبع في درس التفسير - إلى نحو ربع قرن من الزمان - تقليديا أثريا

rows.speaker: أمين الخولي
rows.claim: Amin al-Khūlī broke from the traditional pattern by treating the Qur’an as a linguistic and rhetorical text according to a method he established; the author was among his students.
rows.anchor: حتى جاء شيخنا الإمام "الأستاذ أمين الخولي" فخرج به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Literary tafsīr remained confined to tafsīr courses rather than entering the broader study of Arabic rhetoric and its heritage.
rows.anchor: ولكن التفسير الأدبي للقرآن ظل حتى اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The admission that tafsīr is an underdeveloped Arabic discipline gives the author grounds to enter the field within the limits of her ability and expertise.
rows.anchor: من علوم العربية التي لم تنضج ولم تحترق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects interpretations and approaches she judges distant from authentic Arabic and at odds with the Qur’an’s explicit wording and spirit.
rows.anchor: رفض بعض أقوال لهم وتأويلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an can unite Arabs across environments, dialects, and cultural inheritances, and unite Muslims across countries and languages in belief, law, and way of life.
rows.anchor: نلوذ بكتابنا الأكبر الذي نلتقي عنده لساناً ووجداناً على اختلاف بيئاتنا ولهجاتنا وتباين ميراثنا الحضاري والفني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such unity requires renewed, precise study that penetrates sectarian and doctrinal interpretations and foreign aesthetic tastes to reach the Qur’an’s original core.
rows.anchor: لن يكون هذا التلاقي عند كتابنا العربي المبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book is an attempt to understand the Qur’anic text through Arabic sensibility, attending to every word, vowel, and tone and using the Qur’an itself to resolve disagreement.
rows.anchor: على أن أخلص لفهم النص القرآني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her method tracks the Qur’an’s vocabulary and contextual indications, listening closely to the expressive suggestion of its inimitable discourse.
rows.anchor: على هدى التتبع الدقيق لمعجم ألفاظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The method studies one topic across the whole Qur’an, collecting its instances and learning its normal words and patterns, instead of isolating a word or verse in a sūra-by-sūra reading.
rows.anchor: التناول الموضوعي الذي يفرغ لدراسة الموضوع الواحد فيه، فيجمع كل ما في القرآن منه، ويهتدى بمألوف استعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports about occasions of revelation often mistakenly attach a verse to whatever someone thought caused it; the claimed cause is not necessarily indispensable to revelation.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو معنى قول علماء القرآن: إن المرويات في أسباب النزول يكثر فيها الوهم. ونقدر معه أن السببية فيها ليست بمعنى العلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The default is to apply a verse’s general wording unless explicit text or clear contextual evidence requires considering the specific occasion.
rows.anchor: وأن العبرة في كل حال، بعموم اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order of revelation also matters for understanding the Qur’an’s overall context, word meanings, and rhetorical features across the muṣḥaf.
rows.anchor: والأخرى: أن ترتيب النزول موضع اعتبار كذلك، لفهم السياق العام لما نتدبر من آيات القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsīr cannot supply a word that is equivalent or synonymous with a Qur’anic word in its setting; humans cannot produce a comparable verse.
rows.anchor: لا يعني بحال ما، تقديم كلمة يمكن أن تقوم مقام الكلمة القرآنية في سياقها، على وجه المماثلة والترداف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsīr is only an effort to understand and explain approximately; the lack of an equivalent helps explain exegetes’ lengthy discussions and many interpretive possibilities.
rows.anchor: التفسير ليس إلا محاولة للفهم على وجه الشرح والتقريب، بالكلمات المفسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author acknowledges that her effort is limited and leaves future generations of scholars and students an open field to discover what she could not.
rows.anchor: على تدبر كتابنا الأكبر فتدرك منه ما فاتنا أن ندركه

words: وَمَا أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse that says human knowledge is only a little underscores the limits of human effort and the Qur’an’s inexhaustible secrets.
rows.anchor: ويبقى من أسراره ما يفوت ظاقة البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Few university Arabic professors have made Qur’anic text a subject of systematic study comparable to their study of other texts, despite its unsurpassed rhetoric.
rows.anchor: من حاول أن يجعل من النص القرآني موضوعا لدراسة منهجية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her survey of Arabic department examinations over a quarter-century found no question on Qur’anic rhetoric, showing that the idea had not taken root clearly enough.
rows.anchor: فلم أجد من بينها سؤالا في البيان القرآني، فدل هذا على أن الفكرة لم تأخذ حظها الكافي من الوضوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’anic studies broadly lack a method and are sometimes undertaken by authors unqualified for them.
rows.anchor: والدراسات القرآنية، في المجال العام، تسير على غير منهج، ويتصدى لها من المؤلفين من ليسوا أهلا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She recalls Muṣṭafā Ṣādiq al-Rāfiʿī’s work on the Qur’an’s inimitability and says its value is discussed in her book’s introduction on rhetorical inimitability.
rows.anchor: في إعجاز القرآن، والحديث عن قيمتها يأتي في مدخل كتابي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though she grew up listening to and reciting the Qur’an reverently, she came to grasp its rhetoric only through specialized study of texts and Arabic literary heritage, which made her question her earlier understanding of Arabic.
rows.anchor: ألفت منذ الصغر أن أصغي بكل وجداني إلى هذا القرآن، وأن أتلو آياته في تأثر وخشوع، لكني لم أع بيانه حق الوعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After years of contemplation, the author found Qur’anic rhetorical secrets difficult to express adequately and hesitated to publish until she had devoted her full effort, while recognizing that the subject exceeds human capacity.
rows.anchor: فكنت كلما اجتليت باهر أسراره البيانية، ألفيت من الصعب أن أقدمها على النحو الذي يفي بخلالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The method rigorously surveys each Qur’anic word across all its occurrences and compares stylistic features with parallels throughout the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: بضوابطه الصارمة التي تأخذنا باستقراء اللفظ القرآني في كل مواضع وروده، للوصوص إلى دلالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analysis considers a feature in its immediate verse and sūra as well as in the whole muṣḥaf to uncover its rhetorical purpose.
rows.anchor: وتدبر سياقها الخاص في الآية والسورة، ثم سياقها العام في المصحف كله، التماساً لسرها البياني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic dictionaries and tafsīr serve the method, which seeks a word’s shared semantic core across its different usages.
rows.anchor: نحاول أن ندرك حسن العربية للألفاظ التي نتدبرها من النص القرآني، عن طريق لمح الدلالة المشتركة

none: Publisher book catalog and page number only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some colleagues successfully applied this method to Qur’anic topics in master’s and doctoral theses.
rows.anchor: وقد طبق بعض الزملاء هذا المنهج تطبيقاً ناجحاً، في موضوعات قرآنية اختاروها لرسائل الماجستير والدكتوارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She applies the method to short sūras with thematic unity, most of them Meccan and focused on foundational Islamic teachings.
rows.anchor: وأتجه بمحاولتي اليوم إلى تطبيق المنهج في تفسير

rows.speaker: السلف الصالح
rows.claim: The author follows the early maxim that the Qur’an explains itself, while saying exegetes have not fully realized its implications.
rows.anchor: ويلتزم دائماً قوله السلف الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her inductive, inimitability-centered approach differs from conventional tafsīr and seeks to free Qur’anic meaning from imported elements and distortions.
rows.anchor: توضيح الفرق بين الطريقة المعهودة في التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’anic scholars must first understand the text itself; comparison with the Qur’an exposes strained interpretations in tafsīr, lexicons, and rhetoric that the Qur’an rejects.
rows.anchor: مدى حاجتنا إلى فهم نصه قبل أي شيء آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s rhetoric depends on exact wording, with no substitute for a word or letter and with each vowel and tone occupying its precise place in the composition.
rows.anchor: في اللفظ لا يقوم مقامه سواه، وفي الحرف لا يؤدى معناه حرف آخر، وفي الحركة أو النبرة مكانها في النظم الباهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever reception her attempt receives, she values what it has already given her in spiritual reward and in intellectual, aesthetic, and interpretive understanding through service to the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: فحسبي الذي نلت من ثوابها، وما أجدت على مادة وذوقاً وفهماً، حين انقطعت لخدمة كتاب

none: Contents page listing sūras and page numbers only.
